The must-sees

  • Alte Oper

    Culture · 1880

    It opened in 1880 and was gutted by bombs in 1944. Left a ruin for decades, it was rebuilt by public demand and reopened as a concert hall in 1981.

    Look for: Above the entrance, read the inscription Dem Wahren Schönen Guten, a dedication to truth, beauty and goodness.

  • Frankfurt Cathedral

    Church

    Never a bishop’s seat, it was where German kings were elected and, from 1562, crowned. The tower was rebuilt after a fire in 1867 and can be climbed.

    Look for: Beside the choir, find the small Election Chapel, where the prince-electors met to choose the king.

  • Goethe House

    Museum

    Goethe was born here in 1749 and wrote early works upstairs. The house was destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt; much of the furniture had been taken to safety.

    Look for: Upstairs, find the puppet theatre Goethe played with as a boy.

  • Iron Footbridge

    Bridge · 1869

    Built in 1869, it links the Römerberg with Sachsenhausen. It was blown up at the end of the war and rebuilt soon after.

    Look for: On the iron beam over the walkway, a line from Homer’s Odyssey is written in Greek: sailing the wine-dark sea to men of other tongues.

  • Main Tower

    Viewpoint · 2000

    Completed in 2000, it is one of the few towers in the city open to visitors. From the top you see the whole skyline and the river curving through it.

    Look for: From the top, look east along the river for the European Central Bank: two glass towers joined by a tall atrium.

  • Römer

    Civic building

    The city council bought the house Zum Römer in 1405 and has met here ever since. Upstairs, the Imperial Hall hosted banquets after coronations and is lined with portraits of emperors.

    Look for: The three stepped gables belong to three once separate houses. The town hall grew by buying up its neighbours.

  • Römerberg

    Square

    For centuries newly crowned emperors were celebrated on this square. The gabled houses facing the Römer were rebuilt in the 1980s after their destruction in 1944.

    Look for: On the fountain, Justice holds her scales and sword but wears no blindfold.

  • St. Paul’s Church

    Civic building · 1833

    Completed in 1833, it hosted Germany’s first freely elected national parliament in 1848–49. Burned out in the war, it was rebuilt for the centenary in 1948.

    Look for: In the entrance hall, a long mural by Johannes Grützke shows the members of the 1848 parliament filing in.

  • Städel Museum

    Museum · 1815

    Banker Johann Friedrich Städel left his collection to found it in 1815. The lawn’s skylights light an underground gallery opened in 2012.

    Look for: Find Tischbein’s Goethe in the Roman Campagna: the poet lounging in a white travelling cloak among ancient ruins.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Frankfurt and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Frankfurt passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
